text:
Dylan Cozens was ejected for a high hit on Anaheim's AJ Greer, who went on injured reserve, and the question in Ottawa now is whether a suspension follows. It comes right after Hayden Hodgson served two games for charging the Kings' Brandt Clarke. Two headline hits in two weeks is a pattern people notice, and the Senators take 4.72 penalties a game. They draw 5.17, which is why it hasn't sunk them yet.

The bigger hole is up front. Warren Foegele and Andre Burakovsky are both out three to four weeks, per the Ottawa Citizen and TSN, and Ottawa's top lines have been patched together all season: none of its trios has played even 60 minutes together at five on five. Thomas Chabot and Jordan Spence have been the steady pair, at 60 percent of the expected goals.

At 11-6-1 the Senators are slightly better than even on process (51 percent of the chances) and have Samuel Ersson playing better than his save rate shows, 3.9 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. Our simulations give them a 72 percent playoff chance. The 2-1 win in Buffalo that closed a five-game road trip is what this team looks like when it holds together. Keeping Cozens on the ice is step one.
headline: Ottawa's discipline problem has a name this week
